CVS.thesis_one_line: America's largest drugstore-and-health-insurance company is fixing the Medicare cost overruns that crushed its stock and now trades cheaply, but still carries heavy debt.
kill_criteria: Aetna Medical Benefit Ratio rises above 92% for two consecutive quarters (vs 87.4% in Q2 2026).
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 4.0x, or a second rating agency downgrades CVS below BBB-/Baa3.
A further goodwill impairment is taken against the Health Care Delivery (Oak Street) reporting unit, following the $5.7bn Q3-2025 charge.
FY adjusted EPS guidance is cut from a prior range (breaking the pattern of raises through Q3-2025-Q2-2026).
2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings (expected ~October 2026) show a material reversal from the 81%/63% (4-star/4.5-star) share achieved for 2026.
key_adverse_facts: $5.7bn non-cash goodwill impairment against Health Care Delivery/Oak Street taken in Q3 2025.
Net debt/EBITDA is approximately 3.7x (GAAP-TTM approximation), with a negative ratings outlook from S&P and Fitch (Moody's is stable at Baa3).
FY2026 operating-cash-flow guidance was cut from the December-2025 Investor Day's tease of at least $10.0bn to at least $9.0bn at the official February-2026 guide, before being raised twice since.
Director Larry Robbins (Glenview Capital) sold $317.5 million of CVS stock on 2026-05-19, the largest single disclosed insider transaction in the review period.
Omnicare LLC, a legacy long-term-care pharmacy subsidiary, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on 2025-09-22.
Goodwill of $85.5bn is approximately 75% of current market capitalization.
data_conflicts: No major conflict versus V1 identified. Nuance flagged: a 'guidance raised' headline for FY2026 operating cash flow would be misleading without noting it was first cut relative to the Investor Day preview before being raised twice.
CVS.confidence_in_thesis: medium - the turnaround is evidenced in hard data (MBR improvement, star-rating recovery, three guidance raises in four releases) across multiple quarters, but the pace and magnitude of any multiple re-rating, and the post-2028 PBM cost-plus economics, remain uncertain

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Agree CVS is statistically cheap and the operational turnaround (Aetna MBR, star ratings, guidance raises) is real; disagree with the pace/magnitude of V1's base case, which assumes full re-rating to a ~17.5x exit multiple (near the pre-2024-crisis average) within three years - a more conservative 13-15x still supports a solid but more modest return given 3.7x leverage, $85.5bn of goodwill and the unresolved post-2028 PBM cost-plus mandate.

DVA.thesis_one_line: The largest US dialysis provider is boosting earnings mainly through debt-funded buybacks, not patient growth, while Warren Buffett's Berkshire slowly sells its large stake.
kill_criteria: Normalized non-acquired treatment growth is negative for two consecutive quarters (reversing the +0.1%/+0.3% seen in H1 2026).
Company-defined leverage ratio rises above 4.0x (from 3.37x in Q2 2026).
Berkshire Hathaway's ownership falls below 25% via an accelerated sale (versus a gradual, buyback-driven drift), signalling loss of confidence rather than mechanical float shrinkage.
Full-year adjusted EPS or adjusted operating-income guidance is cut from a prior range (breaking the pattern of raises/maintains through Q1-Q2 2026).
A material adverse ruling or settlement in the Bayne qui tam case, or a formal charge (not just a subpoena/CID) arising from the American Kidney Fund investigations, is disclosed.
key_adverse_facts: Shareholders' deficit (negative equity) of $(651.1) million at year-end 2025.
Company-defined leverage ratio rising, 3.34x (Q1-2026) to 3.37x (Q2-2026), funded partly by two credit-agreement amendments in ten months (November 2025, June 2026).
FY2026 initial guidance implied roughly 32.6% EPS growth versus only about 3.2% operating-income growth at the midpoint - growth is overwhelmingly buyback/non-operating driven, not organic.
Normalized non-acquired treatment growth was -0.6% for full-year 2025, only turning marginally positive (+0.1%, +0.3%) in the first two quarters of 2026.
Berkshire Hathaway (~45% owner) sold shares on 2026-07-31 even as its percentage stake mechanically rises from DaVita's own share buybacks shrinking the float.

An active qui tam False Claims Act suit (Bayne) survived a motion to dismiss in April 2025, and American Kidney Fund-related regulatory investigations have been open since 2020/2023 with no disclosed resolution.
data_conflicts: Q1-2026 'diluted shares outstanding' (68.875 million) and Q2-2026 'shares outstanding' (63.955 million) as reported in the two earnings releases are not on a fully consistent basis (weighted-average diluted vs period-end outstanding) and imply a larger one-quarter share-count drop than the disclosed $348 million / 2.2 million-share Q2 buyback alone would explain. V1's own diluted-share input (66.09 million) sits between the two figures.
DVA.confidence_in_thesis: medium - the buyback-driven EPS growth is real and legal, but depends on continued cheap financing; organic treatment growth is only marginally positive and the long-run GLP-1 effect on the dialysis population remains unresolved

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Agree DVA is statistically cheap versus both its own history and the peer median; flag that the earnings growth underpinning the re-rating case is overwhelmingly buyback/financially engineered (FY2026 guidance implies ~32.6% EPS growth vs only ~3.2% operating-income growth) rather than organic, which makes the base case more fragile to a rise in financing costs or a slowdown in buyback pace than a pure multiple-re-rating story would suggest.

EOG.thesis_one_line: A low-cost US shale oil producer looks cheap, but recent profits are inflated by a war-driven oil price spike that may not last.
kill_criteria: WTI averages below $50/bbl for two consecutive quarters and the regular dividend is cut (the direct test of the company's own disclosed breakeven claim).
Full-year capex guidance is raised without a corresponding production-guidance increase, or the reinvestment rate (capex/OCF) exceeds 70% outside a low-price justification.
The shale-antitrust litigation (In re Shale Oil Antitrust Litigation, D.N.M.) reaches class certification or a quantified potential-damages disclosure appears in a 10-Q/10-K.
Encino/Utica well costs stop improving versus the pre-acquisition run-rate, or the approximately $150 million disclosed synergy target is abandoned or missed.

Total debt rises above $12bn without a corresponding production or proved-reserve increase, a sign buybacks are being funded by leverage rather than cash flow, unlike the current conservative balance sheet.
key_adverse_facts: Q2 2026 realized oil price of $98.18/bbl reflects a live Iran/Strait-of-Hormuz war price spike, not a sustainable level; WTI was still approximately $92-93/bbl at this review's cutoff with the conflict unresolved.
Consensus forward EPS is already below trailing EPS (calendarized FY0 P/E 8.25x vs FY1 P/E 9.41x), i.e. the Street already expects earnings to fall as prices normalize.

EOG is a named defendant, together with seven other shale producers and two former CEOs of other companies, in a consolidated antitrust class action; a motion to dismiss was largely denied on 2026-08-31 and exposure is entirely unquantified.
CFO Ann Janssen is retiring effective 2027-01-01, succeeded by an internal hire with under eighteen months' tenure at the company.
data_conflicts: V1's own model flagged TTM capex as missing/zero in the underlying D3 dataset (proxied with D&A); resolved here with primary-source figures (FY2025 capex approximately $6.3bn, Q2-2026 capex $1,638 million).

V1's bear-case scenario (-70.4%/yr annualized, implying a year-3 share value of $3.66) appears to be a scenario-engine artefact (a multiplicative collapse of both margin and exit multiple in one window) that is difficult to reconcile with EOG's own disclosed sub-$50/bbl breakeven; flagged to the lead as a possible methodology issue for high-operating-leverage commodity names generally, not resolved within this dossier.
EOG.confidence_in_thesis: medium - excellent balance-sheet discipline and a genuinely low breakeven, but current earnings partly reflect a live, unresolved geopolitical oil-price spike and a new, unquantified antitrust-litigation risk

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Disagree on magnitude, not direction: V1's 9.07x multiple and 32.9% TTM EBIT margin input embed the Feb-Jun 2026 Iran/Hormuz war oil-price spike (Q2-2026 realized price $98.18/bbl vs EOG's own approximately $65-73/bbl pre-war range); consensus already prices in normalization (FY0 P/E 8.25x below FY1 P/E 9.41x). On a mid-cycle ~$65-70/bbl deck EOG is fairly valued rather than statistically cheap, though its sub-$50/bbl breakeven still supports inclusion at reduced size.
